'''15''' ('''fifteen''') is the [[natural number]] following [[14 (number)|14]] and preceding [[16 (number)|16]]. {{Infobox number
| number =  15
| numeral = [[pentadecimal]]
| divisor = 1, 3, 5, 15
| lang1 = [[Hebrew numerals|Hebrew numeral]]
| lang1 symbol = <span style="font-size:150%;">ט"ו / י"ה</span>
|lang2=[[Babylonian cuneiform numerals|Babylonian numeral]]|lang2 symbol=𒌋𒐙}}

==Mathematics==
15 is the eighth [[composite number]] and the sixth [[semiprime]] and the first odd and fourth discrete semiprime.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|sequencenumber=A001358|2=Semiprimes (or biprimes): products of two primes.}}</ref> Its proper [[divisor]]s are {{num|1|}}, {{num|3}}, and {{num|5}}, so it is the first semiprime of the form 3 × q,<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A001748|2=a(n) = 3 * prime(n)}}</ref> where q is a higher prime. 15 is a [[deficient number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A005100|deficient numbers}}</ref> because the sum of the proper divisors of 15 is less than 15. The [[prime factor]]s of 15, 3 and 5, form the first [[Twin prime|twin-prime]] pair.  

Because 15 is the product of distinct [[Fermat prime]]s, 3 and 5, a regular [[pentadecagon]] is [[constructible polygon|constructible]] with a compass and unmarked straightedge, and <math>\cos \frac {\pi}{15}</math> is [[constructible number|expressible in terms of square roots]]. 

The first 15 [[superabundant number]]s are the same as the first 15 [[colossally abundant number]]s. There are 15 [[supersingular prime (moonshine theory)|supersingular primes]]. There are 15 [[truncatable prime]]s that are both right-truncatable and left-truncatable:
:2, 3, 5, 7, 23, 37, 53, 73, 313, 317, 373, 797, 3137, 3797, 739397 {{OEIS|id=A020994}}
There are 15 partitions of a set of size 4, making 15 a [[Bell number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000110|Bell or exponential numbers}}</ref>[[File:Cuadrado Mágico.png|thumb|M = 15]]15 is the [[magic constant]] of the unique order-3 [[magic square|normal magic square]].

15 is the first number to be [[Polygonal number|polygonal]] in 3 ways: it is the 5th [[triangular number]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000217 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000217 |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> a [[hexagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000384|Hexagonal numbers}}</ref> and [[Polygonal number#Table of values|pentadecagonal]] number.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A051867|pentadecagonal numbers.}}</ref> It is also a [[centered tetrahedral number]].

15 is a [[lucky number]].[[File:15-square-difference.png|thumb|15 as the difference of two positive squares (in orange).|120x120px]]15 is the smallest positive number that can be expressed as the difference of two positive [[square number|squares]] in more than one way:<ref>{{cite OEIS|A334078|a(n) is the smallest positive integer that can be expressed as the difference of two positive squares in at least n ways.}}</ref> <math>4^2-1^2</math> or <math>8^2-7^2</math> (see image).

In decimal, 15 contains the digits 1 and 5 and is the result of adding together the integers from 1 to 5 (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15). The only other number with this property (in decimal) is [[27 (number)|27]].
:[[File:Chord diagrams K6 matchings.svg|thumb|The 15 perfect matchings of ''K''<sub>6</sub>]]
There are 15 [[perfect matching]]s of the [[complete graph]] ''K''<sub>6</sub> and 15 [[rooted binary tree]]s with four labeled leaves, both of these being among the types of objects counted by [[double factorial]]s.

If a positive definite quadratic form with integer matrix represents all positive integers up to 15, then it represents all positive integers via the [[15 and 290 theorems]].

There are 15 [[Pentagonal tiling#Monohedral convex pentagonal tilings|monohedral convex pentagonal tilings]], with eight being edge-to-edge. There are 15 [[Euclidean tilings by convex regular polygons|regular and semiregular tilings]] when infinite (improper) [[apeirogon]]al forms are counted: three are [[Euclidean tilings by convex regular polygons#Regular tilings|regular]] (with one self-dual), eight are [[Euclidean tilings by convex regular polygons#Archimedean, uniform or semiregular tilings|semiregular]] (with one chiral), and four are [[Order-2 apeirogonal tiling|apeirogonal]] (from a total of 8, in-which 4 are duplicates).

Full [[icosahedral symmetry]] contains 15 mirror planes (2-fold axes). Specifically, the [[symmetry order]] for both the [[regular icosahedron]] and [[regular dodecahedron]] (which is made of [[regular pentagon]]s) is [[120 (number)|120]]: equal to sum of the first 15 integers, and the [[factorial]] of 5, wherein the sum of the first 5 integers itself is 15. Expressed mathematically:
: <math>\sum_{i=1}^{15}i = 120 </math>, while <math>\sum_{i=1}^{5}i = 15 </math>, and <math>5! = 120</math>.

[[Image:Coquina variation3.jpg|thumb|right|185px|[[Seashell]]s from the [[mollusk]] ''[[Donax variabilis]]'' have 15 coloring pattern [[phenotype]]s.]]

==Religion==
===Sunnism===
The [[Hanbali]] Sunni madhab states that the age of fifteen of a solar or lunar calendar is when one's taklif (obligation or responsibility) begins and is the stage whereby one has his deeds recorded.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Spevack|first1=Aaron|title=Ghazali on the Principles of Islamic Spiritualit|date=2011|page=50}}</ref>

===Judaism===
In the [[Hebrew numerals|Hebrew numbering system]], the number 15 is not written according to the usual method, with the letters that represent "10" and "5" (י-ה, ''[[yodh]]'' and ''[[He (letter)|heh]]''), because those spell out [[Names of God in Judaism#Ehyeh|one of the Jewish names of God]]. Instead, the date is written with the letters representing "9" and "6" (ט-ו, ''[[teth]]'' and ''[[waw (letter)|vav]]'').<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nestle |first=E. |date=1884-01-01 |title=ו״ט = 15. |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/zatw.1884.4.1.249/html |journal=Zeitschrift für die Alttestamentliche Wissenschaft |language=de |volume=4 |issue=Jahresband |pages=249–250 |doi=10.1515/zatw.1884.4.1.249 |issn=1613-0103}}</ref>
